title: Texas Live Oak: Ancient Texas Live Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: A tougher inland live oak built for Hill Country droughts. Austin's 500-year Treaty Oak survived a 1989 poisoning; two more stand in Austin and Fort Worth.
intro: Texas Live Oak is the tougher inland cousin of the coastal live oak, built to survive Hill Country droughts and freezes that would kill its Gulf Coast relative. The three the site maps carry more history than botanical fame. Austin's Treaty Oak, reckoned at about 500 years old and known locally as the father of the forest, survived a 1989 poisoning that killed two thirds of it and cost half its crown, then set acorns again eight years later. Nearby, the Battle Oaks are what remains of a larger grove said to have been felled for a Civil War fortification; they nearly fell too, in 1923, to make room for a university building, until a classics professor talked the committee out of it. Fort Worth's Turner Oak kept a farmer's gold buried in its roots through the same war, dug up afterward to help pay off the young town's debts.
